label: sim-ir-index-struggling-2
source: simulated demo student (persona: struggling) run through the real platform

viva.summary: The student understands the purpose of the code and how to modify data structures, but struggles with tracing the logic of nested loops and intersection operations.

rubric.revise_next: Practice dry-running your code on paper with small inputs to better understand how data flows through your functions.

questions.answer: Ye check is liye zaroori hai taake list mein duplicate numbers na ayen, lekin mera khayal hai ye list ko sort karne ke liye 0 return karega.
questions.feedback: You correctly identified that the check prevents duplicates, but the comment about sorting is incorrect.
questions.prompt: In `if i not in index[word]:`, why is this check necessary before appending the doc ID to the list?

questions.answer: Iska answer shayad koi list aayegi jisme apple aur cherry dono honge. Mujhe code thora confuse kar raha hai par lagta hai ye sab match karega.
questions.feedback: You were unable to trace the logic of the intersection function correctly.
questions.prompt: If you call search_and(build_index(['apple banana', 'banana cherry']), 'apple', 'cherry'), what will be the output?

questions.answer: I think we would change the part where we create the list of ids, to instead use a dictionary that keeps count. Also we should change the inner if that checks if i not in index[word] because we don’t need that check when counting frequency.
questions.feedback: You correctly identified the necessary structural changes to transition from a list of IDs to a frequency counter.
questions.prompt: If we wanted to modify the index to store the frequency count of each word instead of a list of doc IDs, which parts of the build_index function would you change?

messages.body: Ustaad, mujhe lagta hai loop sahi hai lekin answer galat aa raha hai. Hint dein?
Aapka code logic mein sahi lag raha hai, lekin return statement mein variable ka naam check karein. Kya aapne wahi variable return kiya hai jisme aapne data store kiya tha?
messages.hint: Python mein variable names case-sensitive hote hain.
